about: Plume surface interaction on Mars: flight observations used to fit and to check models/plumes/surface.py.

msl_sky_crane.source: J. Vizcaino and M. Mehta, 'Quantification of plume-soil interaction and excavation due to the Sky Crane descent stage', AIAA 2015, NTRS 20150002954: Figure 3 (descent track, p. 4), Table 3 (craters, p. 9), Table 4 and Section V (erosion rates, p. 9), Section II (heights, p. 3).
msl_sky_crane.thrust_note: 'about 2800 lbf of thrust for its final descent stage' (p. 2) = 12.45 kN over the four engines left lit below 23 m.
msl_sky_crane.bcf_note: Erosion turns from viscous shear to bearing capacity failure where the ground disappears from view, about 18 m (p. 9); the first plume interaction is seen at 63 m (p. 3).

sources: M. Mehta et al., 'Explosive erosion during the Phoenix landing exposes subsurface water on Mars', Icarus 211 (2011) 172-194: 5 to 18 cm of soil removed under the lander in under 2 s (Conclusions (2)); pulsed jets erode 5 to 20 times faster than steady ones (Conclusions (1)); a 12 cm rock dragged 35 cm (Fig. 16B).

D. H. Plemmons et al., 'Effects of the Phoenix Lander descent thruster plume on the Martian surface', JGR 113 (2008) E00A11: 10 Hz pulses, 45 ms wide; thrusters 0.5 m above the ground at touchdown (0.25 m on the half-scale rig).
NASA/JPL Phoenix Landing press kit (2008), p. 22: twelve thrusters of about 293 N; constant 2.4 m/s descent from about 30 m; engines off when the footpads sense the ground.
Vizcaino and Mehta (2015), p. 2: lift loss from about 5 m at 2.6 m/s; mean impingement pressure about one tenth of Earth's sea level pressure.
phoenix.exit_note: Not published; the MR-107 class nozzle is taken as 6.6 cm across. The pressure check below is insensitive to it at 0.5 m.
phoenix.removed_note: Erosion stopped at the ice table, so the soil the plume could have removed is at least this deep.

soils.about: Soil classes for the fit. p_bcf_Pa_check: the ground pressure above which bearing capacity failure starts, which surface.py computes from MSL at 18 m (a check value only). loose_depth: how deep the loose layer goes before bedrock or ice stops the digging; drawn per world from the range.

jezero_floor.note: Jezero's floor is rocky with thin regolith; the range brackets MSL's craters stopped by bedrock (5 to 7 cm) and Phoenix's 5 to 18 cm over ice. An engineering range, not a survey.
jezero_floor.density_note: Viking lander soils 1.1 to 1.6 g/cm3 (H. J. Moore et al., USGS Professional Paper 1389, 1987); used only to turn eroded volume into mass. (Vizcaino and Mehta's Table 5 implies 390 kg/m3, which looks like a unit slip, so it is not used.)
